title: A Multi-Scale Model of Cardiac Electrophysiology
author: Colleen Clancy
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5nkg5cw

steps.title: Compile Human 1D/2D model
steps.instruction: Navigate to the folder Code\Human_0D1D2DWF\1D2D and compile the program using either the Intel or GCC compiler with the exact command lines provided.

substeps.instruction: Intel compiler: icc masterCompute.cpp -openmp -o oneD ./oneD initial_WTstates.txt stim_param.txt testOutputFolderTWOd
GCC compiler: g++ masterCompute.cpp -fopenmp -o oneD ./oneD initial_WTstates.txt stim_param.txt testOutputFolderONEd

steps.title: Prepare Human stim_param.txt
steps.instruction: Edit stim_param.txt so that it contains ten lines specifying: (1) Na‑blocker drug concentration, (2) Kr‑blocker ratio, (3) basic cycle length (BCL), (4) number of beats for 1D (e.g., 200) or set beat = 1 for 2D, (5) ligand concentrations, (6) cAMKII activity level (expression = 'WT', 'OE', or 'KO'), (7) dimension (1D or 2D), (8) tissue width (tw), (9) tissue length (tl), (10) homogeneous or heterogeneous tissue.

steps.title: Run Human 1D/2D simulation
steps.instruction: Execute the compiled binary with the command ./oneD initial_WTstates.txt stim_param.txt testOutputFolderTWOd (or testOutputFolderONEd if GCC was used). For 1D simulations, read initial_WTstates.txt (corresponding to SS_rabbit_varNames.txt, 206 variables) and obtain outputs in ecgs.txt (column 1 = time, column 2 = ECG) and the time‑course of the AP surface. For 2D simulations, first generate fiber.cell from the 1D run, then run the same command; the program will produce time‑snapshot files for the 2D tissue.

steps.title: Compile Human single‑cell model
steps.instruction: Navigate to Code\Human_0D1D2DWF\Single_Cell and compile using either Intel or GCC with the exact command lines below.

substeps.instruction: Intel compiler: icc masterCompute.cpp -o singlecell ./singlecell initial_WTstates.txt stim_param.txt testOutputFolder
GCC compiler: g++ masterCompute.cpp -o singlecell ./singlecell initial_WTstates.txt stim_param.txt testOutputFolder

steps.title: Run Human single‑cell simulation
steps.instruction: Execute ./singlecell initial_WTstates.txt stim_param.txt testOutputFolder. The program generates: (1) vm_1Hz.txt containing 29 variables (Ca bound to Casqn, Ca SR, Na dyad, Na sl, Na cytosol, K, Ca dyad, Ca sl, Ca cytosol, Vm, etc.), (2) allresult_1Hz.txt with currents I_Ca_store, I_to_store[0], I_Na_store, I_K1_store, Jserca, IKs_store, IKr_store, Jleak[0], Jleak[1], ICFTR, pars1.Incx, and (3) apds_1Hz.txt with beat number and APD90. Use plotall.m to plot voltage or current time courses.

steps.title: Compile Mouse 1D/2D model
steps.instruction: Navigate to Code\Mouse_0D1D2DWF\1D2D and compile with the same Intel or GCC commands used for the Human model.

substeps.instruction: Intel compiler: icc masterCompute.cpp -openmp -o oneD ./oneD initial_WTstates.txt stim_param.txt testOutputFolderTWOd
GCC compiler: g++ masterCompute.cpp -fopenmp -o oneD ./oneD initial_WTstates.txt stim_param.txt testOutputFolderONEd

steps.title: Prepare Mouse stim_param.txt
steps.instruction: Edit stim_param.txt exactly as described for the Human model (ten lines: Na blocker, Kr blocker, BCL, beats, ligand, cAMKII level, 1D/2D, tw, tl, homogeneous/heterogeneous).

steps.title: Run Mouse 1D/2D simulation
steps.instruction: Run ./oneD initial_WTstates.txt stim_param.txt testOutputFolderTWOd (or ONEd). For 1D, read initial_WTstates.txt (same 206‑variable file) and obtain ecgs.txt (time, ECG) and AP surface time course. For 2D, use the fiber.cell generated from the 1D run to obtain 2D time‑snapshot files.

steps.title: Compile Mouse single‑cell model
steps.instruction: Navigate to Code\Mouse_0D1D2DWF\Single_Cell and compile with either:

substeps.instruction: Intel compiler: icc masterCompute.cpp -o singlecell ./singlecell initial_WTstates.txt stim_param.txt testOutputFolder
GCC compiler: g++ masterCompute.cpp -o singlecell ./singlecell initial_WTstates.txt stim_param.txt testOutputFolder

steps.title: Run Mouse single‑cell simulation
steps.instruction: Execute ./singlecell initial_WTstates.txt stim_param.txt testOutputFolder. Outputs are vm_1Hz.txt (Ca bound to Casqn, Ca SR, Na dyad, Na sl, Na cytosol, K, Ca dyad, Ca sl, Ca cytosol, Vm, etc.), allresult_1Hz.txt (I_Ca_store, I_to_store[0], I_Na_store, I_K1_store, Jserca, IKs_store, IKr_store, Jleak[0], Jleak[1], ICFTR, pars1.Incx) and apds_1Hz.txt (beat, APD90). Plot with plotall.m.

steps.instruction: Navigate to Code\Rabbit_0D1D2DWF\1D2D and compile using the same Intel or GCC commands as for the other species.

substeps.instruction: Intel compiler: icc masterCompute.cpp -openmp -o oneD ./oneD initial_WTstates.txt stim_param.txt testOutputFolderTWOd
GCC compiler: g++ masterCompute.cpp -fopenmp -o oneD ./oneD initial_WTstates.txt stim_param.txt testOutputFolderONEd

steps.title: Prepare Rabbit stim_param.txt
steps.instruction: Edit stim_param.txt with the ten required lines (Na blocker, Kr blocker, BCL, beats, ligand, cAMKII level, 1D/2D, tw, tl, homogeneous/heterogeneous) exactly as described for the other models.

steps.title: Run Rabbit 1D/2D simulation

For 1D, use initial_WTstates.txt (206‑variable file) and obtain ecgs.txt (time, ECG) and the 1D ECG time course. For 2D, read the fiber.cell generated from the 1D run and obtain 2D time‑snapshot files.

GCC compiler: g++ masterCompute.cpp -o singlecell ./singlecell initial_WTstates.txt stim_param.txt testOutputFolder

Outputs are vm_1Hz.txt (Ca bound to Casqn, Ca SR, Na dyad, Na sl, Na cytosol, K, Ca dyad, Ca sl, Ca cytosol, Vm, etc.), allresult_1Hz.txt (I_Ca_store, I_to_store[0], I_Na_store, I_K1_store, Jserca, IKs_store, IKr_store, Jleak[0], Jleak[1], ICFTR, pars1.Incx) and apds_1Hz.txt (beat, APD90).
